nodes.summary: An element $s$ of a ring $R$ is a non-zero-divisor when it is neither a left nor a right zero divisor: for every $z \in R$, $zs = 0$ implies $z = 0$ and $sz = 0$ implies $z = 0$.
nodes.title: Non-zero-divisor

nodes.summary: A ring $R$ satisfies the right Ore condition for its non-zero-divisors, so that it has a classical right ring of quotients, when for all $s, t \in R$ with $s$ a non-zero-divisor there are $x, y \in R$ with $x$ a non-zero-divisor and $sy = tx$.
nodes.title: Right Ore ring

nodes.summary: For every field $k$ and every prime $p$, the group algebra $k[\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}]$ of the lamplighter group $\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}$ does not satisfy the right Ore condition for its non-zero-divisors: there are $s$ and $t$ in it, with $s$ a non-zero-divisor, such that $sy = tx$ holds for no $x$ and $y$ with $x$ a non-zero-divisor.
nodes.title: Lamplighter group algebras are not Ore

nodes.summary: There are a field $k$ and a prime $p$ such that the group algebra $k[\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}]$ of the lamplighter group $\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}$ satisfies the right Ore condition for its non-zero-divisors, that is, has a classical right ring of quotients.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.47: some lamplighter group algebra is Ore

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, the lamplighter group $\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}$ is the semidirect product $\left(\bigoplus_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Z}/p\right) \rtimes \mathbb{Z}$, in which $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ acts on the base group by the $n$-th power of the shift $f \mapsto f(\cdot - 1)$.
nodes.title: Lamplighter group

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, the shift is the automorphism $f \mapsto f(\cdot - 1)$ of the base group $\bigoplus_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Z}/p$, the additive group of finitely supported functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/p$, viewed as a multiplicative group.
nodes.title: Shift of the lamplighter base group

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
